_description: Declarative record of every resource in assets/utdmod and its intended semantic role within the Unified Tension Dynamics substrate architecture. This file is documentation only; it is not loaded at runtime.

substrate_variables.A: Activation — transient excitation of the local field
substrate_variables.M: Memory — accumulated history of past activation
substrate_variables.D: Field Depth — structural maturity; persists after memory fades
substrate_variables.B: Baseline — resting equilibrium level of the field

semantic_roles.observer: Exposes existing substrate state. Never writes state.
semantic_roles.actuator: Injects a controlled external input. State evolves from that input via normal equations.
semantic_roles.boundary_modifier: Alters local equation coefficients while present. Removing it restores original dynamics.
semantic_roles.emergent_phenomenon: Arises from the field reaching a specific dynamical regime. Participates as an ordinary actor.

signal_probe.note: Scientific instrumentation. Never creates or destroys field state.

volatile_stim.note: Applies a single instantaneous impulse to the local substrate chunk. Suitable for impulse-response and propagation experiments.

stability_tonic.note: Transiently modifies dissipation and forgetting coefficients. Does not delete existing field state; modifies the governing dynamics while active.

warding_crystal.note: Changes local substrate physics while held or placed. When removed, normal equations resume. Analogous to introducing a controlled field or catalyst.

tension_stabilizer.note: Increases local dissipation. Does not remove state; increases the rate at which activation decays toward baseline.

property_semantics.false: Nominal coupling — node influences local field equations at full structural capacity.
property_semantics.true: Reduced capacity — structural integrity has been compromised; field coupling is below nominal.

ritual_block.note: Persistent infrastructure. Not a ritual object. Players construct engineered dynamical landscapes by placing networks of nodes. The block does not inject activation; it modifies the equations that govern how activation propagates and persists locally.

tension_serpent.note: Emerges when a specific organized dynamical regime is established. After appearing it acts as an ordinary participant in the substrate — contributing movement impulses and territorial behaviour through normal coupling paths. Never directly overwrites substrate state.

tension_wraith.note: Emerges from disordered, high-gradient, or oscillatory field regimes. Represents the field in a fragmentation state. Like the Coherence Serpent it participates rather than controls.

ritual_ambient.semantic: Substrate Node maintaining steady-state field coupling

entity_serpent_attack.semantic: Coherent structure disrupted by external force

penalty_villager_low.semantic: Field energy diffusing through inhabited area

unregistered_sound_files.magic.ogg: Zero-byte placeholder. Retained for compatibility. Not assigned to any sound event because an empty file is not valid OGG and would produce a runtime error if played.

textures.note: All PNG artwork is placeholder. Artwork will be replaced manually. File names must remain stable as they are referenced by model JSON. Do not rename texture files; update their contents instead.

audit_notes.textures/item/ritual_block.png: Correctly used. The item model models/item/ritual_block.json inherits its texture from the block model via 'parent: utdmod:block/ritual_block' rather than declaring a textures key directly. This is standard Minecraft block-item idiom; the PNG is reachable at runtime.
audit_notes.textures/entity/tension_serpent.png: Used directly by the renderer (TensionSerpentRenderer / TensionSerpentModel). Not referenced by JSON models.
audit_notes.textures/entity/tension_wraith.png: Used directly by the renderer (TensionWraithRenderer / TensionWraithModel). Not referenced by JSON models.
audit_notes.textures/entity/*.bbmodel: Blockbench source files. Not loaded at runtime. Stored alongside project for future artwork revision.

design_invariants: No resource implies direct manipulation of a scalar tension value.
Every item occupies exactly one of the four semantic roles: observer, actuator, boundary_modifier, or emergent_phenomenon.
Registry identifiers (item/block/entity/sound names) match ModItems, ModBlocks, ModEntities, and ModSounds exactly and must not change.
Display names and descriptions in lang/ may evolve freely as long as they communicate the substrate architecture.
The feedback loop is: world dynamics → substrate evolves → structures emerge → entities emerge → entities participate → substrate evolves further.
